title: Spec: books CRUD operations (catalog tag) in openapi.yaml
prompt:
Add the five book operations of story S-02 to backend/api/openapi.yaml, then run `cd backend && go generate ./...`. Never edit internal/oas by hand. New operations return 501 through the handler's fallback until the HTTP adapter (a later task) implements them, so nothing else needs to change. backend/check.sh must pass.

Follow the API conventions in CLAUDE.md:
- routes under /api, JSON in and out, camelCase operationIds;
- every operation declares only its success response plus `default: $ref: '#/components/responses/Error'`;
- the possible error statuses go into the operation `description`.
Add a top-level `tags` entry `catalog` (the book catalog: add, read, list, revise and remove books) and give all five operations that one tag. Keep getHealth as it is.

Contract. The domain model, HTTP adapter and e2e tasks build against exactly these names, some of them in parallel with you:

| operationId | Route | Request | Success | Errors (in the description) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| createBook | POST /api/books | body BookInput, required | 201, Book | 400 invalid input (the message names the field), 409 ISBN already exists |
| listBooks | GET /api/books | query author, limit, offset | 200, BookList | 400 invalid query |
| getBook | GET /api/books/{id} | path id | 200, Book | 404 |
| updateBook | PUT /api/books/{id} | path id, body BookUpdate, required | 200, Book (the revised book) | 400, 404, 409 ISBN already exists or version mismatch |
| deleteBook | DELETE /api/books/{id} | path id | 204, no content | 404 |

Parameters:
- `id` (path, required): integer, format int64, minimum 1.
- `author` (query, optional): string. Matches books that have an author exactly equal to it.
- `limit` (query, optional): integer without format (Go int), minimum 1, maximum 100, default 20.
- `offset` (query, optional): integer without format, minimum 0, default 0.
With these bounds, ogen rejects limit=0, limit=101 and offset=-1 with 400 before the handler runs.

Schemas (components/schemas):
- `Book`. Required: id, isbn, title, authors, createdAt, updatedAt, version.
  - id: integer, int64
  - isbn: string, the normalized ISBN-13 (e.g. 9780132350884)
  - title: string
  - authors: array of string
  - publishedYear: integer without format, optional
  - language: string, optional (ISO 639-1)
  - pages: integer without format, optional
  - createdAt, updatedAt: string, format date-time (RFC 3339)
  - version: integer, int64
  The three optional fields are optional and not nullable. ogen then generates OptInt/OptString, and the fields are absent from the JSON when not set.
- `BookInput` (create body): the editable fields. isbn, title and authors are required; publishedYear, language and pages are optional. Same types as in Book.
- `BookUpdate` (update body): the same editable fields plus `version` (integer, int64, required), the version the client last read. Spell the fields out instead of using allOf, so ogen generates a flat struct.
- `BookList`: required `items` (array of Book, sorted by id ascending) and `total` (integer, int64: the number of matching books, ignoring limit and offset).
Neither body has id, createdAt or updatedAt, and BookInput has no version.

Body validation is deliberately left to the domain. Do NOT add minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, minItems or maxItems to the body schemas. The reasons:
- the domain trims title and authors, counts characters in Unicode code points and accepts hyphenated ISBNs (978-0-13-235088-4), so ogen's validation would disagree with it at the edges;
- the domain's errors name the field.
Document the rules in each field's `description` instead:
- isbn: ISBN-13 starting with 978 or 979, with a valid check digit; hyphens and spaces are removed.
- title: 1–300 characters after trimming.
- authors: 1–20 names of 1–200 characters each, after trimming.
- publishedYear: 1450–2100.
- language: two lowercase letters (ISO 639-1).
- pages: 1–10000.

After generating, check internal/oas/oas_server_gen.go. Every operation shares the default Error response, so ogen uses its convenient errors. The expected methods on oas.Handler are:
- CreateBook(ctx, req *BookInput) (*Book, error)
- ListBooks(ctx, params ListBooksParams) (*BookList, error)
- GetBook(ctx, params GetBookParams) (*Book, error)
- UpdateBook(ctx, req *BookUpdate, params UpdateBookParams) (*Book, error)
- DeleteBook(ctx, params DeleteBookParams) error
If ogen generates per-operation union types (e.g. CreateBookRes), the spec breaks one of the conventions above, so fix the spec. Small naming differences that ogen insists on are fine; the later tasks read internal/oas.

title: Security spec review: books API (S-02)
prompt:
Review the S-02 changes to backend/api/openapi.yaml from a security point of view, before the HTTP adapter is built. The changes are the five catalog operations (createBook, listBooks, getBook, updateBook, deleteBook) and the schemas Book, BookInput, BookUpdate and BookList.

Write the report to docs/security/S02-02-books-api-spec.md: findings with severity, rationale and recommendation, plus what is fine as it is. Authentication and authorization are out of scope for this demo. List them once as an accepted risk and don't repeat them per finding.

Design context:
- The domain enforces the body field rules deliberately, not schema keywords, because it trims, counts Unicode code points and normalizes hyphenated ISBNs. The rules: ISBN-13 starting with 978 or 979 with a valid check digit; title 1–300 characters; 1–20 authors of 1–200 characters each; publishedYear 1450–2100; language ^[a-z]{2}$; pages 1–10000. Validation errors become 400 with a message naming the field.
- The spec bounds limit (1–100, default 20), offset (≥ 0, default 0) and the path id (int64, ≥ 1), so ogen rejects bad values before the handler.
- Updates use optimistic concurrency: the client sends `version`, and a mismatch gives 409.
- IDs are sequential int64 values from a counter. Deletes are hard deletes.
- MongoDB stores books under a strict $jsonSchema validator (catalog/0001), as a second line of defense.

Look in particular at:
- Mass assignment: can a client set id, version, createdAt or updatedAt through BookInput or BookUpdate? Does ogen ignore or reject unknown properties, and should the schemas say additionalProperties: false?
- Resource consumption before the domain validates:
  - unbounded strings and arrays in the body (authors with a million entries);
  - whether schema limits (maxItems, maxLength) would help at all, since ogen validates after decoding, compared with a request body size limit.
- Integer handling: out-of-range or non-integer JSON numbers for publishedYear, pages, version and id; int vs int64 on the wire.
- Query parameters: deep offsets (the cost of skip on MongoDB), the length of the author filter, unexpected parameters.
- Error responses: do the documented statuses reveal whether an ID or ISBN exists in a way that matters (enumeration with sequential IDs)? Without auth, note it as accepted where appropriate.
- Whether the error descriptions follow the conventions in CLAUDE.md.

Don't change the spec yourself; it's outside your scope. Propose each change you recommend as a follow-up task in .orch-proposals.json, with severity and rationale:
- spec changes: role api, scope ["backend/api/**", "backend/internal/oas/**"];
- middleware: role backend, e.g. scope ["backend/internal/middleware/**", "backend/internal/server/**"].
backend/check.sh must pass.

title: Catalog domain, use cases and memory repository (test-first)
prompt:
Build the model of the catalog bounded context test-first (red → green → refactor): the domain, the use cases and the in-memory repository, in backend/internal/catalog/{domain,app,adapter/memory}.

The context exists since S-01, which only added backend/internal/catalog/adapter/mongodb (the books schema, migration catalog/0001). Leave that package alone.

Constraints:
- domain and app are pure Go: no oas, net/http, encoding/json or third-party modules (internal/archtest enforces this).
- The gate needs test changes in every package you change, and at least 80% coverage in domain and app.
- A separate task seeds the demo catalog later (it adds domain/demo*.go and app/seed*.go), so don't build seeding. Do include Repository.FindByISBN, which seeding needs.

Ubiquitous language (from story S-02; put it in the package doc comment of domain):
- Book: the aggregate. It has an ID, an ISBN, a title, one or more authors, and optionally a published year, a language and a page count. It tracks createdAt, updatedAt and a version.
- ISBN: a value object holding an ISBN-13. It is a book's natural key.
- Catalog: the set of all books. A client adds a book to it, revises a book, and removes a book from it.

Rules. The domain enforces them itself, so a request is rejected before it reaches the database, and the memory storage behaves like MongoDB:
- ISBN:
  - an ISBN-13 starting with 978 or 979;
  - the check digit must be valid: weights 1,3,1,3,… over the first 12 digits, check = (10 − sum mod 10) mod 10;
  - hyphens and spaces in the input are removed, so 978-0-13-235088-4 is stored as 9780132350884;
  - anything else that isn't an ASCII digit 0–9 makes the ISBN invalid. Don't use unicode.IsDigit, which accepts non-ASCII digits.
- Title and authors:
  - the title is trimmed (strings.TrimSpace), then must be 1–300 characters;
  - each author name is trimmed, then must be 1–200 characters; a book has 1–20 authors;
  - a value that is empty after trimming is invalid;
  - count characters as Unicode code points (utf8.RuneCountInString), as MongoDB's $jsonSchema does.
- Optional fields: publishedYear 1450–2100; language exactly two lowercase ASCII letters (ISO 639-1, so EN, eng, e and e1 are invalid); pages 1–10000.
- ISBNs are unique within the catalog. The repository checks this.
- The repository assigns the ID when the book is added, and it never changes. IDs are never reused, even after a delete.
- A new book has version 1, and createdAt = updatedAt. Each revision increments the version by 1 and sets updatedAt. createdAt never changes.
- Revising a book replaces all its editable fields (ISBN, title, authors, year, language, pages); an optional field missing from the revision is removed. The client must send the version it last read; if the stored version differs, the revision is rejected (optimistic concurrency).
- Removing a book deletes it for good (no soft delete).

Contract. The HTTP adapter, the repository contract suite, the MongoDB repository and the demo seeding build against exactly these names:
```go
package domain // orch-test/backend/internal/catalog/domain

type BookID int64 // > 0 once added

type ISBN string // only produced by ParseISBN (repositories convert stored values back)
func ParseISBN(raw string) (ISBN, error) // errors are *ValidationError{Field: "isbn"}
func (i ISBN) String() string

// BookDraft: a book's editable fields as a client sends them, not validated yet.
type BookDraft struct {
    ISBN          string
    Title         string
    Authors       []string
    PublishedYear *int    // nil = not set
    Language      *string // nil = not set
    Pages         *int    // nil = not set
}

// Book is the aggregate. Only NewBook and Revise create or change one; repositories rebuild it from storage as is.
type Book struct {
    ID            BookID // 0 until the repository adds the book
    ISBN          ISBN
    Title         string
    Authors       []string
    PublishedYear *int
    Language      *string
    Pages         *int
    CreatedAt     time.Time
    UpdatedAt     time.Time
    Version       int64
}

func NewBook(draft BookDraft, now time.Time) (Book, error) // validated and normalized; ID 0, Version 1, CreatedAt = UpdatedAt = now
func (b *Book) Revise(draft BookDraft, version int64, now time.Time) error

var (
    ErrInvalid         = errors.New("invalid input") // every *ValidationError matches it via errors.Is
    ErrNotFound        = errors.New("book not found")
    ErrDuplicateISBN   = errors.New("a book with this ISBN already exists")
    ErrVersionConflict = errors.New("version conflict: the book was changed since it was read")
)

// ValidationError names the invalid field by its API name: isbn, title, authors, publishedYear, language, pages, limit, offset.
type ValidationError struct{ Field, Reason string }
func (e *ValidationError) Error() string        // "<Field>: <Reason>", e.g. "isbn: invalid check digit"
func (e *ValidationError) Is(target error) bool // true for ErrInvalid

const (
    DefaultLimit = 20
    MaxLimit     = 100
)
type Page struct{ Limit, Offset int }
func NewPage(limit, offset int) (Page, error) // limit 1..MaxLimit, offset >= 0, else *ValidationError (limit or offset)

type ListFilter struct{ Author string } // "" = all books, else books with an author exactly equal to Author

type Repository interface {
    // Add stores b (b.ID is ignored), assigns the next ID and returns the stored book. IDs are > 0,
    // increasing and never reused; gaps are allowed. ErrDuplicateISBN if another book has b.ISBN (then nothing is stored).
    Add(ctx context.Context, b Book) (Book, error)
    Get(ctx context.Context, id BookID) (Book, error)        // ErrNotFound
    FindByISBN(ctx context.Context, isbn ISBN) (Book, error) // ErrNotFound
    // List returns one page of the books matching f, sorted by ID ascending (never nil), and the number of all matching books.
    List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter, p Page) ([]Book, int64, error)
    // Update replaces the stored book b.ID with b if its stored version is still expectedVersion.
    // ErrNotFound, ErrVersionConflict, or ErrDuplicateISBN (another book has b.ISBN); on error nothing changes.
    Update(ctx context.Context, b Book, expectedVersion int64) error
    Remove(ctx context.Context, id BookID) error // ErrNotFound
}
```
```go
package app // orch-test/backend/internal/catalog/app

type ListQuery struct {
    Author string // "" = no filter
    Limit  int    // 1..100; the HTTP adapter fills in the default 20
    Offset int    // >= 0
}
type BookPage struct {
    Items []domain.Book // never nil
    Total int64
}

// UseCases is the catalog's inbound port.
type UseCases interface {
    AddBook(ctx context.Context, draft domain.BookDraft) (domain.Book, error)
    GetBook(ctx context.Context, id domain.BookID) (domain.Book, error)
    ListBooks(ctx context.Context, q ListQuery) (BookPage, error)
    ReviseBook(ctx context.Context, id domain.BookID, draft domain.BookDraft, version int64) (domain.Book, error)
    RemoveBook(ctx context.Context, id domain.BookID) error
}

type Option func(*Service)
func WithClock(now func() time.Time) Option // default time.Now
func NewService(repo domain.Repository, opts ...Option) *Service
var _ UseCases = (*Service)(nil)
```

Behavior:
- NewBook validates the fields in the order isbn, title, authors, publishedYear, language, pages and returns the first *ValidationError. It stores the normalized ISBN, the trimmed title and the trimmed author names. It copies slices and pointers, so later changes to the draft don't leak into the book.
- Revise validates the draft first; if it's invalid, it returns the *ValidationError. Then, if version != b.Version, it returns ErrVersionConflict. In both cases b is unchanged. On success it replaces all editable fields (a nil optional field removes it), increments Version and sets UpdatedAt = now. ID and CreatedAt stay unchanged.
- The Service reads the clock once per use case, as clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond). MongoDB stores milliseconds, so a book read back equals the one returned on write.
- AddBook: NewBook → repo.Add → return the stored book (with its ID).
- GetBook: repo.Get.
- ListBooks: NewPage(q.Limit, q.Offset) → repo.List(ListFilter{Author: q.Author}, page) → BookPage with non-nil Items.
- ReviseBook: repo.Get(id) (ErrNotFound) → b.Revise(draft, version, now) → repo.Update(ctx, b, version) → return the revised book. A concurrent writer gives ErrVersionConflict at the Update step.
- RemoveBook: repo.Remove.
- Return domain errors as they are or wrapped with %w. The HTTP adapter maps them with errors.Is/errors.As: *ValidationError → 400 with its message, ErrNotFound → 404, ErrDuplicateISBN and ErrVersionConflict → 409.

Memory repository: package memory, orch-test/backend/internal/catalog/adapter/memory, with `func NewRepository() *Repository` implementing domain.Repository (`var _ domain.Repository = (*Repository)(nil)`).
- Guard everything with a sync.Mutex, so it's safe for concurrent use. Keep a map[BookID]Book, an ISBN index and a sequence counter.
- Add increments the counter only after the duplicate check. Remove never decrements it, so IDs are never reused.
- Deep-copy Authors and the pointer fields on the way in and out, so callers can't mutate stored books.
- List matches the author exactly (case-sensitive, slices.Contains) and sorts by ID. total counts all matches; then apply offset and limit. An offset past the end gives an empty, non-nil slice.
- Update checks the stored version against expectedVersion, and the ISBN index (the book's own ISBN is fine). When the ISBN changes, it moves the index entry.

Tests:
- domain:
  - table tests for ParseISBN: 978-0-13-235088-4 → 9780132350884; spaces; wrong check digit; 12 and 14 digits; letters; 977 prefix; empty; non-ASCII digits;
  - table tests for every boundary of NewBook: title of 1, 300 and 301 runes, 300 × "ä" is valid, whitespace-only title, trimming; 0, 1, 20 and 21 authors, an empty or whitespace author, names of 200 and 201 runes; year 1449, 1450, 2100, 2101; language en valid, EN, eng, e and e1 invalid; pages 0, 1, 10000, 10001;
  - assert errors.Is(err, ErrInvalid) and the Field;
  - Revise: success, version conflict, invalid draft, removal of optional fields;
  - NewPage boundaries.
- app: use a fake clock with either the memory repository (an external app_test package may import adapter/memory) or a hand-written fake. Cover: timestamps truncated to milliseconds in UTC; add + get round trip; duplicate ISBN; list paging and filter; an invalid page → ErrInvalid; revise not found, stale version, concurrent writer (a fake repository whose Update returns ErrVersionConflict) and success; remove.
- memory: the basic behavior, including that IDs aren't reused after Remove and that stored books aren't aliased. A later task adds the repository contract suite shared with MongoDB.

backend/check.sh must pass.

title: Demo catalog and SeedDemo use case (test-first)
prompt:
Add the demo catalog and the SeedDemo use case to the catalog context, test-first.

The domain, the use cases and the memory repository are merged. Read backend/internal/catalog/domain, app and adapter/memory first, and reuse their test helpers instead of redeclaring them in the same package.

Only add the files in your scope: domain/demo.go + domain/demo_test.go and app/seed.go + app/seed_test.go. The gate needs test changes in both packages; keep coverage at 80% or more. domain and app stay pure Go.

Domain language (story S-02): the *demo catalog* is a fixed list of real books that can be *seeded* into an environment. Seeding is idempotent: a demo book whose ISBN is already in the catalog is skipped, so restarting doesn't create duplicates.

Ambiguity: the story's rule also says "a demo book a user edited or deleted is not restored", but its acceptance criterion says otherwise. Per the criterion, a deleted demo book *is* added again on the next seeding (it's missing by ISBN), and an edited one that kept its ISBN is left as it is. Follow the acceptance criterion; it's the simplest reading: seeding decides by ISBN only, and there are no tombstones. So a demo book whose ISBN an edit changed is seeded again as well. Document this on SeedDemo.

Contract (the bootstrap task and the e2e tests build against it):
```go
// domain/demo.go
// DemoCatalog returns the demo catalog as drafts, in the order of the table below. Each call returns fresh values.
func DemoCatalog() []BookDraft

// app/seed.go
type SeedReport struct {
    Seeded  []domain.Book // the books added, in demo-catalog order, with their IDs
    Skipped []domain.ISBN // the demo books already in the catalog
}
// SeedDemo adds every demo book whose ISBN is not in the catalog yet, through AddBook, so every demo book passes the domain rules.
func (s *Service) SeedDemo(ctx context.Context) (SeedReport, error)
```
SeedDemo is a method of *Service only. Don't add it to the UseCases interface, because it isn't an HTTP operation. It doesn't log; the caller (bootstrap) logs the report.

SeedDemo goes through the demo drafts in order. For each one:
1. ParseISBN.
2. repo.FindByISBN: if the book is found, it's skipped.
3. On domain.ErrNotFound, s.AddBook(draft): the book is seeded.
4. If AddBook returns domain.ErrDuplicateISBN (another instance seeded it at the same moment), it's skipped.
Any other error stops seeding and is returned together with the report so far, wrapped with the ISBN: fmt.Errorf("seed demo book %s: %w", isbn, err).
Calling FindByISBN first matters: with MongoDB, a failed Add still consumes a counter value, so detecting existing books through Add would burn 12 IDs per restart.

The demo catalog. All ISBNs have valid check digits; authors are separated by ", "; — means not set:
| ISBN | Title | Authors | Year | Lang | Pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9780321125217 | Domain-Driven Design | Eric Evans | 2003 | en | 560 |
| 9780321834577 | Implementing Domain-Driven Design | Vaughn Vernon | 2013 | en | 656 |
| 9780321127426 | Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture | Martin Fowler | 2002 | en | 560 |
| 9780134757599 | Refactoring | Martin Fowler | 2018 | en | 448 |
| 9780132350884 | Clean Code | Robert C. Martin | 2008 | en | 464 |
| 9780135957059 | The Pragmatic Programmer | David Thomas, Andrew Hunt | 2019 | en | 352 |
| 9781449373320 | Designing Data-Intensive Applications | Martin Kleppmann | 2017 | en | 616 |
| 9780134190440 | The Go Programming Language | Alan A. A. Donovan, Brian W. Kernighan | 2015 | en | 380 |
| 9781942788331 | Accelerate | Nicole Forsgren, Jez Humble, Gene Kim | 2018 | en | 288 |
| 9780262510875 | Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs | Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman | 1996 | en | 657 |
| 9780465026562 | Gödel, Escher, Bach | Douglas R. Hofstadter | 1999 | en | — |
| 9782070612758 | Le Petit Prince | Antoine de Saint-Exupéry | — | fr | — |
The last two leave optional fields empty on purpose, so the demo shows both shapes. Keep the UTF-8 spellings (Gödel, Saint-Exupéry).

Tests:
- domain:
  - there are 12 drafts, and every one passes NewBook;
  - the ISBNs are distinct and normalized as listed;
  - spot-check fields, including that Gödel, Escher, Bach has no pages, and Le Petit Prince has neither year nor pages;
  - two calls don't share slices or pointers.
- app (with the memory repository or a fake):
  - an empty catalog → 12 seeded, 0 skipped, IDs ascending in table order;
  - a second run → 0 seeded, 12 skipped, still 12 books;
  - after removing one demo book → 1 seeded, 11 skipped;
  - a demo book that was revised but kept its ISBN is left as it is: seeding doesn't change its title or version;
  - Add returning ErrDuplicateISBN → skipped;
  - any other repository error → returned, and its message mentions the ISBN.

backend/check.sh must pass.

title: Repository contract suite (repotest), run against the memory repository
Catalog HTTP adapter, handler embedding, bootstrap wiring and SEED_DEMO_DATA
prompt:
Implement the five catalog operations over HTTP and wire the catalog context into the app with in-memory storage, including demo seeding at startup.

Already merged:
- the spec: operations createBook, listBooks, getBook, updateBook, deleteBook; schemas Book, BookInput, BookUpdate, BookList;
- the catalog model: domain, app, adapter/memory, and Service.SeedDemo.
Read backend/api/openapi.yaml, the generated method signatures in backend/internal/oas/oas_server_gen.go and backend/internal/catalog/{domain,app} first.

The MongoDB repository is a later task. Leave choosing it for STORAGE=mongo to that task (see step 3).

Contracts you build against (in the catalog packages):
- domain:
  - BookID int64; ISBN (String()); BookDraft{ISBN, Title string; Authors []string; PublishedYear *int; Language *string; Pages *int};
  - Book{ID, ISBN, Title, Authors, PublishedYear, Language, Pages, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt time.Time, Version int64};
  - DefaultLimit = 20;
  - the errors: *ValidationError (Field, Reason; Error() = "<field>: <reason>"; matches ErrInvalid), ErrNotFound, ErrDuplicateISBN, ErrVersionConflict.
- app:
  - UseCases{AddBook(ctx, BookDraft) (Book, error); GetBook(ctx, BookID) (Book, error); ListBooks(ctx, ListQuery{Author string; Limit, Offset int}) (BookPage{Items []Book; Total int64}, error); ReviseBook(ctx, BookID, BookDraft, version int64) (Book, error); RemoveBook(ctx, BookID) error};
  - NewService(repo domain.Repository, opts ...Option) *Service;
  - (*Service).SeedDemo(ctx) (SeedReport{Seeded []domain.Book; Skipped []domain.ISBN}, error).
- adapter/memory: NewRepository() *Repository.

1. The driving adapter: package httpapi, at backend/internal/catalog/adapter/httpapi.
```go
type CatalogHandler struct{ uc app.UseCases }
func NewCatalogHandler(uc app.UseCases) *CatalogHandler
```
It implements the catalog methods of oas.Handler. Expected signatures (use what ogen actually generated):
- CreateBook(ctx, *oas.BookInput) (*oas.Book, error)
- ListBooks(ctx, oas.ListBooksParams) (*oas.BookList, error)
- GetBook(ctx, oas.GetBookParams) (*oas.Book, error)
- UpdateBook(ctx, *oas.BookUpdate, oas.UpdateBookParams) (*oas.Book, error)
- DeleteBook(ctx, oas.DeleteBookParams) error
Use cases:
- createBook → uc.AddBook(draft) → 201 with the Book.
- listBooks → uc.ListBooks(app.ListQuery{Author: params.Author.Or(""), Limit: params.Limit.Or(domain.DefaultLimit), Offset: params.Offset.Or(0)}) → BookList{Items, Total}. Items must be a non-nil slice, so an empty catalog renders `items: []`.
- getBook → uc.GetBook(domain.BookID(params.ID)).
- updateBook → uc.ReviseBook(id, draft, req.Version) → 200 with the revised Book.
- deleteBook → uc.RemoveBook(id) → 204.
Mapping:
- oas.BookInput/BookUpdate → domain.BookDraft. Optional fields: a set Opt* becomes a pointer to the value; an unset one becomes nil.
- domain.Book → oas.Book: ID as int64, ISBN.String(), nil optional fields as unset Opt*, CreatedAt and UpdatedAt as they are, Version.
Errors, all mapped in one function:
- errors.As *domain.ValidationError → 400 with its Error() message, which names the field (e.g. "title: …");
- errors.Is domain.ErrNotFound → 404;
- domain.ErrDuplicateISBN → 409;
- domain.ErrVersionConflict → 409.
For 404 and 409, use the sentinel's own message (domain.ErrX.Error()), never err.Error() of a wrapped error, so repository details don't leak. Return &oas.ErrorStatusCode{StatusCode: …, Response: oas.Error{Error: msg}}. Return any other error unchanged; handler.NewError turns it into a 500 without details.
Unit-test the adapter with a fake app.UseCases: each mapping, optional fields present and absent, the defaults for limit and offset, and each error → status.

2. backend/internal/handler/handler.go:
- Embed `*cataloghttp.CatalogHandler` in Handler, next to fallback (import orch-test/backend/internal/catalog/adapter/httpapi as cataloghttp), and update the doc comment. Its methods then take precedence over the 501 fallback.
- Keep GetHealth and NewError. The existing handler tests must keep passing.

3. backend/internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:
- Config gets two fields: `SeedDemoData bool` (add the demo catalog at startup) and `Logger *slog.Logger` (nil means slog.Default()). Also pass the logger to mongodb.MigrateOptions{Logger: …}.
- ConfigFromEnv reads SEED_DEMO_DATA with strconv.ParseBool. Unset, or anything that doesn't parse as true, means false. Update its doc comment.
- In New, wire the catalog after the storage switch, so with STORAGE=mongo it runs after the migrations:
```go
var catalogRepo catalogdomain.Repository = catalogmemory.NewRepository()
// STORAGE=mongo: the MongoDB repository is selected here (next task).
catalogSvc := catalogapp.NewService(catalogRepo)
h.CatalogHandler = cataloghttp.NewCatalogHandler(catalogSvc)
```
  Keep `_ = db` (or an equivalent comment), so the next task can add `if db != nil { catalogRepo = catalogmongo.NewRepository(db) }` before NewService.
- If cfg.SeedDemoData is set, call report, err := catalogSvc.SeedDemo(ctx) after the wiring.
  - On error, close the app and return fmt.Errorf("seed demo data: %w", err): startup fails.
  - Log each seeded book at debug level: logger.DebugContext(ctx, "seeded demo book", "id", …, "isbn", …, "title", …).

title: MongoDB book repository (counters, optimistic locking) and storage switch
prompt:
Implement the catalog's MongoDB repository in backend/internal/catalog/adapter/mongodb, and select it in bootstrap.New when STORAGE=mongo.

The package (package mongodb) already holds the S-01 schema: Migrations(), catalog/0001, BooksCollection = "books".

Already merged; read them first:
- the domain: domain.Repository, Book, ISBN, the errors, Page, ListFilter;
- the memory repository;
- the contract suite backend/internal/catalog/adapter/repotest (repotest.Run);
- the bootstrap wiring of the catalog with the memory repository.

The domain.Repository contract:
```go
type Repository interface {
    // Add stores b (b.ID is ignored), assigns the next ID and returns the stored book. IDs are > 0,
    // increasing and never reused; gaps are allowed. ErrDuplicateISBN if another book has b.ISBN (then nothing is stored).
    Add(ctx context.Context, b Book) (Book, error)
    Get(ctx context.Context, id BookID) (Book, error)        // ErrNotFound
    FindByISBN(ctx context.Context, isbn ISBN) (Book, error) // ErrNotFound
    // List returns one page of the books matching f, sorted by ID ascending (never nil), and the number of all matching books.
    List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter, p Page) ([]Book, int64, error)
    // Update replaces the stored book b.ID with b if its stored version is still expectedVersion.
    // ErrNotFound, ErrVersionConflict, or ErrDuplicateISBN (another book has b.ISBN); on error nothing changes.
    Update(ctx context.Context, b Book, expectedVersion int64) error
    Remove(ctx context.Context, id BookID) error // ErrNotFound
}
```
New in this package:
```go
const CountersCollection = "counters"
// NewRepository returns the MongoDB domain.Repository. The schema must be migrated (catalog/0001).
func NewRepository(db *mongo.Database) *Repository
var _ domain.Repository = (*Repository)(nil)
```

Storage mapping. The books collection has a strict $jsonSchema validator with additionalProperties: false; read booksSchema() in migrations.go. A document has exactly these fields:
- _id: long (int64), the BookID
- isbn: string, normalized
- title: string
- authors: array of strings
- publishedYear: int, optional
- language: string, optional
- pages: int, optional
- createdAt, updatedAt: date
- version: long
Use a document struct. As CLAUDE.md says, use int64 for the long fields and int for the int fields (the driver writes a Go int that fits as BSON int32). Mark the optional fields `omitempty` (e.g. *int), so unset fields are absent, never null. Keep the mapping in one place (toDoc/fromDoc).

Behavior:
- Add:
  - Take the next ID atomically from the counters document {_id: "books", seq}: FindOneAndUpdate on CountersCollection with filter {_id: "books"}, update {$inc: {seq: int64(1)}}, upsert, returning the document after the update.
  - Then InsertOne the book with _id = seq. IDs are therefore never reused, even after a delete. An insert that fails leaves a gap, which the contract allows.
  - If the counter upsert itself fails with a duplicate key error (the two very first Adds racing), retry it once. Never report it as ErrDuplicateISBN.
  - A duplicate key error (E11000, mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError) from the insert on the isbn_unique index → domain.ErrDuplicateISBN. A duplicate _id (the counter is behind existing data) is an internal error, not a duplicate ISBN; tell the two apart by the index name in the write error.
- Get / FindByISBN: FindOne by _id / isbn. mongo.ErrNoDocuments → domain.ErrNotFound.
- List:
  - The filter is {} or {authors: author}. Equality on an array field matches any element exactly and uses the authors_lookup index.
  - The author is always a plain string value inside a bson.D, never decoded into an operator.
  - Sort {_id: 1}, Skip offset, Limit limit. total = CountDocuments with the same filter. Return a non-nil slice.
- Update:
  - ReplaceOne with filter {_id: b.ID, version: expectedVersion} and the full document. Replace, don't $set: a revision that drops an optional field must remove it.
  - MatchedCount 0 → look the ID up: missing → ErrNotFound, otherwise ErrVersionConflict.
  - E11000 on isbn_unique → ErrDuplicateISBN.
  - The version filter makes concurrent updates safe: of two updates with the same expected version, exactly one matches.
- Remove: DeleteOne by _id. DeletedCount 0 → ErrNotFound.
- Wrap other driver errors with context (fmt.Errorf("…: %w", err)). The HTTP adapter turns them into a generic 500.

No schema change is needed: S-01 created the collection, the validator and the indexes. The counters collection needs no migration either; the upsert creates it. If you find the schema must change, that's a new migration catalog/0002 appended to Migrations(). Never edit catalog/0001.

Tests, in package mongodb. They skip without MONGO_TEST_URI. Use the existing newTestDB(t) from testdb_test.go (one database per test), and migrate each database first, e.g. with platformmongo.Migrate(ctx, db, [][]platformmongo.Migration{Migrations()}, platformmongo.MigrateOptions{}).
- repository_test.go: repotest.Run(t, func(t *testing.T) domain.Repository { db := newTestDB(t); migrate it; return NewRepository(db) }).
- MongoDB-specific tests:
  - a stored document passes the S-01 validator: Add succeeds for a complete and for a minimal book;
  - its raw BSON has _id and version as int64, publishedYear and pages as int32, and no fields beyond the schema;
  - the counters document {_id: "books"} has seq equal to the last assigned ID, and keeps counting after a Remove;
  - two or more concurrent Updates of the same book with the same expected version → exactly one succeeds, the others get ErrVersionConflict;
  - an Update that drops an optional field removes it from the document.

Bootstrap:
- In New, select the repository before the service is built: `if db != nil { catalogRepo = catalogmongo.NewRepository(db) }`. Remove the `_ = db` placeholder.
- Keep the seeding after it, so it runs after the migrations.
- Add a MongoDB-gated bootstrap test, following the pattern of TestNewWithMongoStorageMigrates: New with StorageMongo, create a book through app.Handler (httptest + POST /api/books), and find it in the books collection.

If a MongoDB is reachable, run `make test-mongo` (MONGO_TEST_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017 backend/check.sh); `make mongo` starts one. backend/check.sh must pass in any case.

title: e2e: books CRUD acceptance criteria (memory storage)
prompt:
Write end-to-end tests for the S-02 books API in backend/e2e/catalog_crud_test.go (package e2e_test). They run against the fully wired app with in-memory storage (bootstrap.New → handler → catalog httpapi → app → memory repository), through the generated client oas.Client.

Other agents write catalog_storage_test.go, catalog_seed_test.go and security_*_test.go in the same package in parallel, and books_schema_test.go already uses the `books` prefix. So prefix every top-level identifier in your file with `crud` (helpers and tests, e.g. TestCrudCreateCompleteBook, crudServer). You may use newClient(t) from e2e_test.go, but don't change other files.

The API contract (backend/api/openapi.yaml; read it and internal/oas for the exact Go types), all under the catalog tag:
| Operation | Route | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| createBook | POST /api/books | 201, the book | 400 invalid input, 409 ISBN already exists |
| listBooks | GET /api/books?author=&limit=&offset= | 200, {items, total} | 400 invalid query |
| getBook | GET /api/books/{id} | 200, the book | 404 |
| updateBook | PUT /api/books/{id} | 200, the revised book | 400, 404, 409 ISBN already exists or version mismatch |
| deleteBook | DELETE /api/books/{id} | 204 | 404 |

Details:
- A book has id, isbn, title, authors, publishedYear, language, pages, createdAt, updatedAt (RFC 3339) and version. The optional publishedYear, language and pages are absent when not set.
- The create body (BookInput) has the editable fields. The update body (BookUpdate) has the editable fields plus version.
- List is sorted by ID ascending; limit is 1–100 (default 20), offset ≥ 0 (default 0). author matches books with an author exactly equal to it. total counts the matching books, ignoring limit and offset.
- Errors are {"error": "<message>"}. The client returns them as *oas.ErrorStatusCode: use errors.As, then StatusCode and Response.Error. A 400 from the domain names the field in its message (e.g. "title: …").
- Field rules: ISBN-13 with prefix 978 or 979 and a valid check digit, hyphens and spaces removed; title 1–300 characters after trimming; 1–20 authors of 1–200 characters each after trimming; publishedYear 1450–2100; language two lowercase letters; pages 1–10000.

Helpers you'll need:
- A server helper that returns both the client and the base URL (httptest). The generated client may refuse to send some invalid values (e.g. limit=0); if so, send that request with net/http and check the status and the JSON error body.
- A helper for valid ISBN-13s: 978 + 9 digits from n + the check digit. The check digit uses weights 1,3 alternating over the first 12 digits: check = (10 − sum mod 10) mod 10.

Cover each of these acceptance criteria with at least one test named after it, and quote the criterion in a comment above the test:

Create
- Given an empty catalog, when I create a complete, valid book, then I get 201 with `id`, `version` 1 and `createdAt` = `updatedAt`, and `GET /api/books/{id}` returns the same book.
- Given a book with only the required fields, when I create it, then I get 201 and the optional fields are absent from the response.
- Given the ISBN `978-0-13-235088-4`, when I create a book, then it is stored and returned as `9780132350884`.
- Given a book whose ISBN is already in the catalog, also in a different spelling (with hyphens), when I create it, then I get 409 and the catalog is unchanged.
- Given an ISBN with a wrong check digit, 12 or 14 digits, letters, or starting with `977`, when I create a book, then I get 400 with a message naming `isbn`.
- Given an empty or whitespace-only title, a 301-character title, no authors, 21 authors, an empty author name, year 1449 or 2101, pages 0 or 10001, or language `EN` or `eng`, when I create a book, then I get 400 with a message naming the field.

Read and list
- Given no book with ID 999, when I get it, then I get 404.
- Given 25 books, when I list without parameters, then I get the first 20 by ID and `total` 25; with `offset=20` I get the remaining 5.
- Given books by several authors, when I list with `author=Martin Fowler`, then I get only books that have exactly that author, and `total` counts only those.
- Given `limit=0`, `limit=101` or `offset=-1`, when I list, then I get 400.
- Given an empty catalog, when I list, then I get 200 with `items: []` and `total` 0.

Update
- Given a book with version 1, when I update it with version 1 and a new title, then I get 200 with the new title, version 2, an `updatedAt` later than or equal to before, and an unchanged `createdAt`.
- Given a book now at version 2, when I update it with version 1, then I get 409 and the book is unchanged.
- Given two books, when I change the first one's ISBN to the second one's, then I get 409.
- Given no book with ID 999, when I update it, then I get 404. Invalid fields give 400, as for create.

Delete
- Given a book, when I delete it, then I get 204, and getting it afterwards gives 404.
- Given no book with ID 999, when I delete it, then I get 404.
- Given a deleted book, when I create a new book, then it gets a new ID, never the deleted one's.

Notes:
- "The catalog is unchanged" / "the book is unchanged": check with listBooks total and getBook after the failed call.
- Field errors: one subtest per case in the criterion, each asserting 400 and a message that contains the field's API name (isbn, title, authors, publishedYear, language, pages). Also send a few of the same invalid bodies through updateBook.
- Author filter: include a book with several authors, one of them Martin Fowler, and near misses such as "martin fowler" and "Martin Fowler Jr.", which must not match.
- `items: []`: check the raw JSON from net/http contains an empty array, not null.
- 25 books: create them with distinct valid ISBNs; IDs ascend in creation order.
- Compare times with Equal.

If a test fails because the implementation is wrong, don't weaken it. Keep the test, skip it with t.Skip naming the bug, and propose the fix in .orch-proposals.json (role backend, with the scope of the faulty package). backend/check.sh must pass.
